canonical.name: The defining Dirichlet series names zeta only on the half-plane Re s greater than 1
The eta identity is a representation theorem and may not be used by dividing through the zeros of 1-2^(1-s)
At s = 1 the defining Dirichlet series becomes the harmonic series and so does not define zeta there
The Jacobi theta function is theta(t)=sum over all integers of exp(-pi n^2 t) for t greater than 0
The theta reciprocity used for zeta is the Poisson-summation identity for the scaled Gaussian under the fixed Fourier normalization
This page writes Lambda(s)=pi^(-s/2) Gamma(s/2) zeta(s), while xi(s)=1/2 s(s-1)Lambda(s) is the entire completion
Lambda is meromorphic with poles at 0 and 1, whereas xi is entire
The Euler-product proof here agrees with the published infinitude-of-primes theorem instead of replacing it
Bernoulli numbers are fixed by t/(e^t-1)=sum B_n t^n/n! with B_1=-1/2
The classical Basel identity via the sine product is already published on the earlier entire-functions page and is reused rather than duplicated here
The Riemann hypothesis is mentioned here only as an open-problem seam and not scaffolded as a proved zeta-page item
canonical.reason: The CA-22 design explicitly treats the Riemann hypothesis as an external open-problem mention rather than a local theorem. This batch records that future page destination instead of minting an unproved zeta-page statement.
